interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary: Scotland’s electrical network is operating under deep green generation conditions, anchored by a robust 4.4 GW of wind generation that continues to dominate the regional energy supply. This surge in renewable dispatch has successfully suppressed Scottish carbon intensity to an exceptionally clean 32 gCO2/kWh, positioning the national grid well ahead of broader decarbonization milestones. However, this high-yield generation environment simultaneously exposes structural transmission and export bottlenecks across the network. Across the current operating window, total wasted energy has mounted to 221.1 MWh, driven primarily by localized circuit congestion and thermal transfer limits restricting flow across the Anglo-Scottish boundary toward southern demand centers. While system stability and near-zero emission thresholds remain intact, the scale of curtailed volume underscores persistent market inefficiency and lost economic value. To bridge the gap between high generation capacity and transmission constraints, system stakeholders must accelerate the deployment of co-located battery storage, dynamic line rating, and flexible industrial demand-response assets. Maximizing these flexibility levers will be essential to capturing surplus megawatt-hours, mitigating costly curtailment actions, and converting stranded wind energy into actionable, resilient grid capacity.
